RE:      Waterloo and Seneca Falls Hydroelectric Project, FERC Project No. 2438
         October 2026 Article 405 Deviation Reporting

Dear Secretary Reese,

Kleinschmidt Associates, on behalf of C-S Canal Hydro LLC, licensee for the Waterloo and
Seneca Falls Project (FERC No. 2438) on the Seneca River in New York, is filing this Article
405 Deviation Report for the month of October 2026.

October 2026 Article 405 Reporting

During the month of October 2026, the level of Seneca Lake was below the target
elevation. The precipitation received for the month of October was between 25% and 50%
of the normal precipitation expected for the area where the Waterloo and Seneca Falls
Project is located, and is a continuation of the trend of lower-than-average precipitation
values since June, when rainfall totals began to decline. Lower water levels are typical for
this time of year depending on precipitation, and are consistent with this time in 2025,
2022, 2020, and 2016. The ongoing trend of low precipitation over several months has
brought the elevation of Seneca Lake down naturally while, as required by License Article
405, C-S Canal Hydro has discharged flows adequate to maintain minimum flow
obligations, navigation flows, and the elevation of Van Cleef Lake, which the level of
Seneca Lake is subordinate to.

Throughout the month of October 2026, the level of the Cayuga-Seneca Canal has been
in compliance with the requirement to be maintained no lower than 0.5 ft below the
Seneca Lake elevation. The data for the Cayuga-Seneca Canal from approximately 9:15
AM to 12:00 PM on October 28, 2026, indicate a short-duration drop in elevation followed
by a quick recovery to the normal elevation. This was caused by a drawdown of the power
canal at the Waterloo station to accommodate a New York State Department of

                                                                                          KleinschmidtGroup.com
 Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
November 10, 2026                                                                                           2.


Transportation (NYSDOT) bridge inspection of the Washington Street Bridge, located
immediately upstream of the power canal. The transducer that records the elevation of
the Cayuga-Seneca Canal is located in the power canal at the Waterloo Station, and was
therefore affected by the canal dewatering activities. During the drawdown, the required
flow and elevation in the Cayuga-Seneca Canal was maintained by opening a bypass gate.
There was no actual deviation in the Cayuga-Seneca Canal during this time. The data in
the spreadsheet was manually adjusted to reflect the location of the balance of flows
during the DOT drawdown. The drawdown was approved by the NYSDEC and USFWS.
Consultation documentation is included in Attachment E.

Throughout October 2026, the level of Van Cleef Lake was maintained at approximately
429.2 ft. This is slightly higher than the target elevation range as established in the Order
Granting Temporary License Variance dated November 12, 2025, and extended to January
20, 2027 by Order dated October 23, 2026 1. As discussed in an email from the Licensee
to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) New York Regional Office (NYRO)
dated June 1, 2023, the slightly higher elevation is necessary to avoid impacts to docks
owned by residents and the Town of Seneca Falls, a local golf course, and an industrial
facility that had process water restrictions imposed. NYSCC also indicated that the lower
elevation in Van Cleef was causing impacts to navigation operations. The target elevation
for Van Cleef Lake has been slightly higher than the variance elevation, at approximately
429± ft since June 2023.

October 15 Comment of Seneca Lake Pure Waters Association

On October 15, 2026, William H. Roege of the Seneca Lake Pure Waters Association filed
comments regarding the October 10, 2026, Article 405 Deviation Report (Report). Mr.
Roege identified a discrepancy in a figure used in the Report, as well as discrepancies in
the flow data reported. Mr. Roege’s comments led to a minor correction to the report that
included updating the precipitation figure in Attachment C, and corrections to the Excel
spreadsheet of data. The Excel files for July, August, and September were corrected and
provided with the response to the comments provided on November 9, 2026. The
corrections included separating column M to show the difference between the leakage
flow, bypass flow, and turbine leakage values, and removal of the misaligned gate leakage
at the downstream Seneca Falls development from the data that had been mistakenly
used as the leakage value since the gate became misaligned in July. As discussed in the
comment response, the 164 - 175 cfs gate leakage is occurring at the downstream Seneca
Falls development and should not have been included in the upstream Waterloo leakage

value. As a result, the flows reported out of the Waterloo development have been adjusted
for the months of July, August, and September to show the correct leakage conditions at
Waterloo. This was strictly a reporting error and did not affect actual flows; minimum
environmental and navigational flow requirements continued to be met throughout this
period. Stakeholder correspondence related to the elevation of Seneca Lake is included
in Attachment F, and is being filed as privileged due to the presence of stakeholders’
personal information, such as personal email addresses or cell phone numbers.

 REGULATORY             BACKGROUND LICENSE ARTICLE: ART405: The licensee shall operate the Waterloo and Seneca Falls
 REQUIREMENTS:          Project to control fluctuations of the reservoir surface elevation at each development for the protection of
                        wetlands, wildlife, and fish habitat and recreational opportunities in the project impoundments. The
                        licensee shall act at all times to maintain the impoundment water surface elevations, as measured at the
                        agreed upon gage location, as follows:

                        Maintain the Seneca Lake impoundment within ±0.3 foot of the seasonal target elevations of 446.0 feet
                        BCD during the summer and 445.0 feet BCD during the winter. During flood control events the
                        impoundment upper limit is +0.55 foot. The elevation of Seneca Lake is subordinate to the
                        maintenance of the water levels for navigation and minimum flow to sustain Van Cleef Lake
                        elevations. As excepted below when Seneca Lake levels drop below 445.9 feet BCD summer and 444.9
                        feet BCD winter, the Seneca Falls Powerhouse will be placed in a no discharge non-power generation
                        status. The Waterloo powerhouse will operate to discharge flows required to maintain the navigation
                        levels and minimum flow for Van Cleef Lake.

                        The Seneca Lake transition from winter to summer takes place in a 20-day period beginning March 1 and
                        a transition from summer to winter in a 45-day period beginning November 1. For the transition periods
                        the target increments of daily change in elevation are: summer +0.053 foot and winter -0.023 foot. The
                        transitions are conditioned on any surplus or deficiency of precipitation.

                        Maintain Van Cleef Lake impoundment at a target elevation of 430.5 feet BCD with a maximum daily
                        water level fluctuation of ±0.25 foot. During the non-navigation season (December 1 to April 30), when so
                        requested by local authorities and after consultation with the New York State Canal Corporation (NYSCC)
                        Van Cleef Lake may be drawn down to an absolute minimum of 425.5 feet BCD by the operation of the

               Seneca Falls powerhouse to aid local flood control. As needed, the Seneca Falls powerhouse will operate
               due to local runoff to control the navigation level of Van Cleef Lake.

               The Waterloo development maintains the Cayuga-Seneca Canal portion of the Waterloo impoundment as
               measured in close proximity to the powerhouse, at the location described in the approved flow
               monitoring plan required by section B.6 of the modified Water Quality Certification, such that the surface
               water elevation does not fluctuate more than 0.5 foot below the daily average surface elevation as
               measured at the NYSCC Geneva gage on Seneca Lake. The daily average surface elevation to be used is
               the average elevation of the previous calendar day at the Geneva gage.

               The licensee may vary from the recommended water level management regime for Seneca Lake, the
               Seneca Canal portion at the Waterloo Impoundment, and/or for Van Cleef Lake due to circumstances
               beyond the control of the licensee (flood control or emergency conditions) and for short periods of time
               upon mutual agreement with the NYSCC, with notification to the New York State Department of
               Environmental Conservation Regional Permit Administrator within 5 days. If the water level management
               regime for Seneca Lake, the Waterloo impoundment, and/or Van Cleef Lake is so modified, the licensee
               shall notify the Commission as soon as possible, but not later than 10 calendar days after the end of the
               month in which each incident occurred.
EVENT              • The elevation of Seneca Lake was below target during October 2026 due to abnormally low
DESCRIPTION             precipitation in the region. C-S Canal Hydro has discharged flows adequate to maintain minimum
AND CAUSE:              flow obligations, navigation flows, and the elevation of Van Cleef Lake, which the level of Seneca
                        Lake is subordinate to.
                   • Throughout October 2026 the level of the Cayuga-Seneca Canal remained in compliance with the
                        requirement to be maintained no lower than 0.5 ft below the Seneca Lake elevation. One drop in
                        the data on October 28, 2026 is explained by the NYSDOT bridge inspection of the Washington
                        Street Bridge just upstream of the Waterloo power canal. The transducer measuring the Cayuga-
                        Seneca Canal elevation is located in the Waterloo power canal, and therefore appeared to drop
                        the Cayuga-Seneca Canal elevation below target. The Cayuga-Seneca Canal remained in
                        compliance while only the power canal was drawn down for the bridge inspection. Required flow
                        and elevation in the Cayuga-Seneca Canal was maintained by opening a bypass gate. The data in
                        the spreadsheet was manually adjusted to reflect the location of the balance of flows during the
                        DOT drawdown.
                   • Throughout October 2026 the level of Van Cleef Lake was maintained at approximately 429.2 ft.
                        This is slightly higher than the target elevation range as established in the Order Granting
                        Temporary License Variance dated November 12, 2025, and extended to January 20, 2027, by
                        Order dated October 23, 2026 (Accession Number 20261023-3014). As discussed in an email from
                        the Licensee to FERC NYRO dated June 1, 2023, the slightly higher elevation is necessary to avoid
                        impacts to docks owned by residents and the Town of Seneca Falls, a local golf course, and an
                        industrial facility that had process water restrictions imposed. NYSCC also indicated that the lower
                        elevation in Van Cleef was causing impacts to navigation operations. The target elevation for Van
                        Cleef Lake has been slightly higher than the variance elevation, at approximately 429± ft since
                        June 2023.

CORRECTIVE     As required by the License Article 405, when the elevation of Seneca Lake reached 445.9, the Licensee
MEASURES:      placed the Seneca Falls powerhouse in a no discharge, non-power-generation status, and operated the
               Waterloo powerhouse to maintain the elevation of Van Cleef Lake. Minimum flows were maintained
               throughout the reporting period.

Hello All,

On behalf of C-S Canal Hydro LLC, a subsidiary of Relevate Power LLC, I am writing to
inform you of a drawdown of the power canal at the Waterloo Station on the Cayuga-
Seneca Canal. The purpose of the drawdown is to allow NYDOT access for their
annual inspection of the piers and abutments of the Washington Street Bridge located
immediately upstream of the powerhouse. It is anticipated that the drawdown will begin
today, 10/27/26, and it is expected that the canal will be fully rewatered by Friday,
10/30/26. The drawdown is planned to be accomplished through the operation of the
Tainter gates at the head of the power canal in order to isolate the inspection area.
Water is being passed through bypass gate #6 to maintain the water levels in Van Cleef
Lake.

Personnel will be onsite for the entire duration of the drawdown to address any potential
fish stranding concerns.

Please feel free to reach out to me at this email address, or Jonathan Dollard (Chief
Dam Safety Engineer) at jdollard@relevatepower.com with any questions.
 Thank you,

Sydney Robinson
Staff Regulatory Consultant
